claims.text: A computational method based on DFT phonon-dispersion calculations can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
DFT-based phonon-dispersion calculations can be used to predict phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
Phonon thermal conductivity is a critical property for thermal-insulation applications.
Phonon dispersion relations influence thermal conductivity.
DFT-based calculations accurately predict phonon dispersion relations in high-entropy alloys.
Accurate phonon-dispersion predictions permit identification of materials with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed method will improve the accuracy of identifying high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
More accurate identification of low-phonon-conductivity alloys will lead to better thermal-insulation performance.
Current predictions of phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys are inaccurate.
The approach is limited to high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications where phonon thermal conductivity is dominant.
The accuracy of DFT-based calculations is uncertain for complex high-entropy alloy systems.
TDTR or LFA can be used to obtain experimental phonon thermal-conductivity values for the benchmark alloys.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted values differ by more than 10% from experimental measurements for a majority of the tested alloys.
